title: wheel-crypto-scan record
description: One record per wheel. Evidence only: no field of this document asserts FIPS compatibility, and the verdict taxonomy has no passing class. Consumers must ignore unknown keys; added optional keys and added rule ids do not bump schema_version, while removing or retyping a field does.

ruleset_version.description: Bumped on any policy change; part of the scan cache key.

analyzer_version.description: Bumped when extraction behaviour changes for an unchanged wheel.

evidence_level.description: Which evidence level produced this record. At 'minimal' the matched_symbols, matched_strings and rust_crates arrays are not recorded, so an empty array means 'not recorded' rather than 'none found'.

filename.description: Basename only. No host path ever appears in a record.

name.description: Null when the wheel's metadata could not be read.

source_available.description: True only when at least one .py file was actually parsed. When false, the absence of Python findings means nothing.

bundled_libs.description: Native libraries shipped inside the wheel by auditwheel or delocate.

py_files_unparsed.description: How many .py files could not be parsed. When this equals py_files, Layer 3 produced nothing and source_available is false.

binaries_truncated.description: True when the binaries and extensions lists were capped, so a wheel with thousands of objects cannot produce an unbounded record.

vendored_path.description: True when the object lives in an auditwheel or delocate vendor directory.

stripped.description: No .symtab, or a Mach-O with no LC_SYMTAB entries. ELF reads the declared count; Mach-O reads what the table yielded, so an nsyms of zero over rows the object does carry is a table we could not use and sets partial_analysis instead of this. Never set for PE, whose own symbol table is debug information every linker drops.

symtab.description: .symtab entries for ELF, LC_SYMTAB entries for Mach-O, and for PE the things the object named, one per import thunk and one per export slot, because PE has no symbol table of its own.

matched_symbols.description: Empty at --evidence-level minimal. binding is the key field: imported means the code lives elsewhere, defined means this object carries it.

partial_analysis.description: True when part of the object was not read. This is the field to filter on; partial_reasons says which causes applied, and the two always agree. A fat Mach-O whose every slice read cleanly is not partial: the slices merge into one record.

partial_reasons.description: Sorted, deduplicated reasons the object was not read in full. Present whenever this tool produced the record, and empty exactly when partial_analysis is false. Not every reason records a matching entry in errors: several are routine rather than failures. New values may appear without a schema_version bump.

items.description: no_structural_reader: this tool has no reader for the format, so the object was scanned for strings alone; elf_header_unread: the ELF header itself would not parse; elf_section_table_truncated: the ELF header parsed but the section header table it points at does not fit the object; elf_sections_unread: a section header could not be read, so anything derived from the section list may be missing rather than absent: needed, soname, rpath, runpath, the symbol counts and the strings alike; elf_section_data_unread: a section's bytes could not be read, so the strings pass ran over less than the object holds; elf_dynamic_unread: .dynamic would not resolve, so needed, soname, rpath and runpath are empty because they could not be read, not because the object declares none; elf_dynsym_unread: .dynsym would not read, named strings .dynstr does not hold, or declared fewer entries than .dynstr holds names for, so the imported-versus-defined split is missing or partial; elf_symtab_unread: .symtab would not read, so stripped and symbol_counts.symtab describe a table we failed on rather than one the object does not have; elf_go_buildinfo_unread: .go.buildinfo would not read, so Go toolchain provenance is missing; macho_header_unread: the Mach-O header, or a fat header, would not parse; macho_symtab_incomplete: LC_SYMTAB was absent, declared no entries, or declared entries this reader could not take at their word: unreachable, naming strings it does not hold, holding nothing but debug records, or declaring fewer entries than the string table holds names for. It records an error unless the table left nothing unexplained -- an absent LC_SYMTAB, or one declaring no entries over a string table holding no name it failed to account for -- and that error says which way it fell short. stripped and symbol_counts.symtab then describe a table we could not use rather than one the object does not have; macho_fat_slice_unread: a slice of a universal binary could not be read, or its header named one it did not describe; pe_header_unread: the PE header chain would not parse; pe_section_table_truncated: the section table was cut short, so an address may resolve to the wrong bytes; pe_no_import_directory: no import directory, or one naming no DLL, so the object declared no dependency; records no error; pe_import_incomplete: an import directory that was there and could not be walked in full; pe_export_incomplete: an export directory that was there and could not be read in full; pe_ordinal_import: an import named by ordinal alone, so its function has no name to match; routine on Windows, and records no error; pe_ordinal_export: an export the name table never points at: a definition with no name; records no error; pe_delay_load: a delay-load import directory, which this reader does not parse, so the libraries it names are undeclared dependencies; records no error; symtab_understates_rows: A symbol table declared fewer entries than the string table it points into holds names for, so symbols the object carries were never looked at. The object is not corrupt: every structural check passes and the count is simply not the truth. Emitted by the ELF and Mach-O readers alike, beside that format's own cause, because the lie and the check are the same in both.

findings.description: One entry per rule and subject, not per occurrence.

rule_id.description: Stable identifier from the ruleset. New ids may appear without a schema_version bump.

subject.description: The matched table entry: a crate, library, module or distribution.

severity.description: Strength of the evidence, not a compatibility judgement.

layer.description: Current values: metadata, binary, python, derived. New layers may be added without a schema_version bump.

occurrences.description: Number of distinct locations, not raw matches: two calls on one line count once.

truncated.description: True when the locations list was capped; occurrences still holds the full count of distinct locations.

evidence.description: The literal matched evidence, printable ASCII, capped.

subject_kind.description: What kind of thing `subject` names: distribution, library, crate, module, symbol_group, string_group, constant, attribute, component, generator or format. Null when the finding has no subject. New values may appear without a schema_version bump.

class.description: The highest-precedence class that fired. Always equals classes[0].

classes.description: Every class that fired, in precedence order.

conditions.description: Resolved conditions, keyed <library>_linkage. openssl_linkage is always present and is the field that distinguishes a wheel linking the system OpenSSL from one carrying its own.

errors.description: Non-fatal failures. A populated errors array means part of the wheel was not examined.

stage.description: Current values: archive, metadata, binary, python. New stages may be added without a schema_version bump.

binaryFormat.description: Current values: elf, macho, pe, unknown. New formats may be added without a schema_version bump.

verdictClass.description: There is deliberately no passing class. The tool never emits a passing verdict, under any name. Current values: NON_APPROVED_CRYPTO, FIPS_BREAKING, CONDITIONAL, CONTEXT_DEPENDENT, OPAQUE, NO_CRYPTO_DETECTED. New classes may be added without a schema_version bump; the authoritative list is the ruleset's [verdict] precedence. There is deliberately no passing class.
